strings.name: Christine Lagarde
strings.summary: Christine Lagarde moved from commercial law into the French government and later led the IMF and European Central Bank. She participated in international coordination and monetary policy during financial crises, the pandemic and rising inflation, while advocating women's participation in economic decisions. Policies are made collectively; her handling of the Tapie arbitration as finance minister also led to judicial scrutiny.
strings.coverageNote: Sources checked through 13 November 2026; events reach the departure announcement of 29 October 2026. Departure on 7 February 2027 is planned, not completed. Monetary policy is a Governing Council decision, not a personal act.
strings.facts.fact-01.label: Birthplace
strings.facts.fact-02.label: Education
strings.facts.fact-02.value: Postgraduate commercial and labor law studies, Paris X University
strings.facts.fact-03.label: Associated organizations
strings.facts.fact-03.value: European Central Bank; IMF; French government; Baker McKenzie
strings.highlights.highlight-01.title: Leading international institutions
strings.highlights.highlight-01.text: Became the IMF's first woman managing director in 2011 and European Central Bank president in 2019.
strings.highlights.highlight-02.title: Crisis response and monetary policy
strings.highlights.highlight-02.text: During her ECB presidency, the Governing Council introduced pandemic bond purchases and later adjusted rates as inflation increased.
strings.timeline.event-01.title: Announces planned early departure
strings.timeline.event-01.text: Notified institutions of plans to leave on 7 February 2027; she had not departed by this profile's review date.
strings.timeline.event-02.title: ECB begins interest-rate adjustment
strings.timeline.event-02.text: The Governing Council raised three key rates by 50 basis points and approved the Transmission Protection Instrument.
strings.timeline.event-03.title: Pandemic emergency purchases
strings.timeline.event-03.text: The ECB Governing Council announced an initial €750 billion PEPP to address the pandemic shock.
strings.timeline.event-04.title: Becomes ECB president
strings.timeline.event-04.text: Succeeded Mario Draghi, leading the ECB and participating in euro-area monetary-policy decisions.
strings.timeline.event-05.title: Found negligent in the Tapie case
strings.timeline.event-05.text: A French court found her failure to challenge the arbitration payment negligent, but imposed no penalty.
strings.timeline.event-06.title: Becomes IMF managing director
strings.timeline.event-06.text: Became the institution's first woman leader and served until 2019.
strings.timeline.event-07.title: Becomes French finance minister
strings.timeline.event-07.text: Moved from trade and agriculture into economic and financial governance before the global financial crisis.
strings.timeline.event-08.title: Leads an international law firm
strings.timeline.event-08.text: Elected chair of Baker McKenzie's global executive committee, overseeing international legal operations.
strings.timeline.event-09.title: Enters commercial legal practice
strings.timeline.event-09.text: Worked in commercial, merger, competition and labor law, developing an international law-firm career.
strings.timeline.event-10.title: Born in Paris
strings.timeline.event-10.text: Born in Paris, France, later pursuing law and economics-related education.
strings.influence.rationale: Led the IMF and ECB, participating in global financial stability and monetary-policy coordination.
